interest: For diplomatic and political historians, this file provides an invaluable, month-by-month record of the crucial diplomatic breakdown that set the United States and Japan on an irreversible course toward war in late 1940 and early 1941. The reports offer rare, contemporaneous eyewitness insights into the domestic implementation and friction surrounding Prince Konoye's 'New National Structure,' the bureaucratic struggles of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, and the tightening of totalitarian controls over religious missions, foreign press outlets (such as the sale of the Japan Advertiser), and the domestic economy. Additionally, the presence of internal Division of Far Eastern Affairs digest memoranda alongside multiple overlapping copies and comprehensive monthly schedules of embassy telegrams and despatches provides scholars with a clear view of how information flowed, was distilled, and was indexed within the State Department during an escalating international crisis.
overview: This archival file forms the second part of State Department decimal file 894.00 (File 1247), spanning August 1940 to February 1941 across 573 pages and 38 documents, centered on comprehensive monthly reports on conditions in Japan (Reports Nos. 167, 168, 169/1669/1670, 1671, and 1672) compiled by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo, accompanied by Division of Far Eastern Affairs analytical memoranda and extensive registers of outgoing telegrams and despatches. The documents chronicle the precipitous deterioration of Japanese-American relations following Japan’s signing of the Tripartite Pact, U.S. scrap iron embargoes, the congressional introduction of Lend-Lease, and State Department advisories urging American citizens to evacuate the Far East. In parallel, the file charts Japan’s aggressive southward expansion into French Indochina, pressure on the Netherlands East Indies, aerial campaigns targeting the Burma Road, and mediation in the Thai-Indochina conflict, while providing detailed reporting on the internal transformation of the Japanese state under Prime Minister Konoye’s 'New National Structure,' the inauguration of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, and sweeping economic, agricultural, and civil mobilization under wartime legislation.
